applies_why: The judge text compares the defender's chain answers against the challenger's chain press and concludes neither chain forces the other, which is the chain-against-chain task the rule governs.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse -- I weighed reading it as requiring whole-chain support comparison against reading it as only banning isolated contrary-verse citations; the judge text's neither chain forces the other follows the whole-chain comparison.
why: The judge resolves the Acts 2:30 collision by setting the defender's loins/legal-flesh chain against the challenger's named-Davidic-man chain as wholes and finding neither forces the other, so it does not use a verse-by-verse or stating-verse test.
